lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use barbed/stinging trichomes, many stamens and an inferior one-locular ovary with parietal placentation to make the herbaceous Cornales branch memorable.

project_scope.note: The project contains Cevallia sinuata and Mentzelia oligosperma. Cevallia represents the true stinging-hair door; Mentzelia represents the barbed stickleaf door.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Inspect the hairs before touching. Loasaceae commonly has rough, barbed, hooked or stinging trichomes. Then confirm a 5-part bisexual flower with many stamens and an inferior usually one-locular ovary with parietal placentation.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Annual/perennial herbs to subshrubs; leaves usually alternate, simple and often lobed/toothed; stipules absent. Surface hairs may be scabrid, glochidiate, barbed or stinging.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and radial, commonly 5 sepals + 5 petals. Stamens range from 5 to very many and can be arranged in bundles; petaloid staminodes may occur. Ovary inferior, usually one-locular with parietal placentation.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a capsule opening by apical valves or longitudinally; persistent sepals common.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Rough/barbed or stinging plant + showy 5-part flower + many stamens + inferior capsule is the Loasaceae package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: hair type → 5-part flower → many stamens → inferior ovary → capsule → Cevallia/Mentzelia split
visual_lesson.intro: Loasaceae is the 'look before you touch' Cornales family. Hair architecture gets you close; the inferior ovary and many-stamen flower finish the call.

steps.title: 1 · Cevallia door: true stinging hairs
steps.look_for: Long stiff stinging hairs mixed with dense pubescence on stems/leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: This separates Cevallia from Mentzelia and creates a useful comparison with Urticaceae and stinging Euphorbiaceae.

steps.title: 2 · Mentzelia door: barbed stickleaf hairs
steps.look_for: Barbed or retrorsely hooked hairs that cling to clothing/skin but are not the same as Cevallia's true stinging hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: The hair mechanism is a practical genus-level split.

steps.title: 3 · Count the stamens
steps.look_for: A 5-petaled flower with numerous stamens; outer filaments may be broadened or petaloid in some Mentzelia groups.
steps.why_it_matters: Moves the ID beyond hair texture into reproductive structure.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm the inferior ovary
steps.look_for: Perianth and stamens appear above an ovary embedded below the flower; placentation is parietal in a single main locule.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the key Cornales connection and separates the family from Urticaceae.

steps.title: 5 · Follow it to a capsule
steps.look_for: Dry capsule opening by apical valves or along the fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: Completes the family pattern and separates it from Cornus drupes.

comparisons.title: Loasaceae vs Urticaceae
comparisons.rule: Stinging hairs overlap. Loasaceae has bisexual showy 5-part flowers, numerous stamens and an inferior ovary/capsule; Urticaceae has tiny mostly unisexual flowers, superior one-ovuled ovaries and achenes.

comparisons.title: Loasaceae vs Hydrangeaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can show many stamens and inferior ovaries. Loasaceae is typically rough/barbed/stinging and herbaceous; project Hydrangeaceae is a woody opposite-leaved mock-orange shrub.

comparisons.title: Cevallia vs Mentzelia
comparisons.rule: Cevallia sinuata uses true stinging hairs; Mentzelia uses barbed stickleaf hairs that grab rather than inject.

visual_lesson.caveat: Not every Loasaceae species stings. Mentzelia is specifically valuable because it teaches the barbed-hair, non-stinging family pathway.

genera.fast_cue: stinging hairs + narrow yellow/orange flower parts + inferior ovary
barbed stickleaf hairs + 5 petals + many stamens + inferior capsule

visual_targets.structure: Cevallia stinging hair vs Mentzelia barbed hair
visual_targets.annotation_goal: side-by-side true stinging hair and retrorsely barbed trichome
label petals, fertile stamens and any broadened outer filaments
